title: What Is XLM?
description: Understand the native asset of the Stellar network and its role in powering transactions and accounts.

content.prompt: What is the native digital asset of the Stellar network, used to pay transaction fees and maintain minimum account balances?

hint: Its ticker symbol starts with X and it is also called the Lumen.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Creating a Stellar Account
description: Learn how Stellar accounts are created and what the minimum balance requirement is.

content.prompt: What is required to activate (create) a Stellar account on the network?
options: Fund it with the minimum base reserve in XLM
Register a username on the Stellar website
Obtain approval from a validator node

solution: Fund it with the minimum base reserve in XLM
hint: Stellar accounts must hold a minimum number of XLM to exist on the ledger.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Public and Secret Keys
description: Understand the keypair structure that identifies Stellar accounts.

content.prompt: In Stellar, what does the public key (account ID) represent?
options: The account's address shared with others to receive payments
The private password used to sign transactions
The hash of the last transaction

solution: The account's address shared with others to receive payments
hint: Think of the public key as your bank account number — safe to share publicly.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Transaction Fees on Stellar
description: Discover how Stellar calculates transaction fees and why they are kept intentionally low.

content.prompt: How is the transaction fee determined on Stellar?
options: By multiplying the base fee (100 stroops) by the number of operations in the transaction
By a fixed flat fee of 1 XLM per transaction
By an auction between miners competing for block space
By the total value transferred in XLM

solution: By multiplying the base fee (100 stroops) by the number of operations in the transaction
hint: One stroop equals 0.0000001 XLM. Fees scale with complexity, not value.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: What Is a Stroop?
description: Learn the smallest unit of XLM and how it relates to transaction fees.

content.prompt: One XLM equals how many stroops?

hint: 1 XLM = 10^7 stroops. The base fee is 100 stroops.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Stellar Operations
description: Explore the building blocks of Stellar transactions: operations.

content.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a valid Stellar operation type?

hint: Stellar does not use Proof of Work, so there is no mining involved.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Minimum Account Reserve
description: Understand the base reserve mechanism that prevents spam on the Stellar network.

content.prompt: What is the purpose of the base reserve requirement on a Stellar account?
options: To prevent spam accounts and ensure network quality
To pay validators for securing the network
To cover the cost of Soroban smart contract execution
To fund the Stellar Development Foundation

solution: To prevent spam accounts and ensure network quality
hint: By requiring a minimum balance, the network disincentivises the creation of throwaway accounts.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Stellar Consensus Protocol (SCP)
description: Learn how the Stellar network reaches consensus without mining.

content.prompt: What consensus mechanism does the Stellar network use?

hint: Stellar uses a unique trust-based consensus model invented by David Mazières called FBA.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Quorum Slices in SCP
description: Understand the role of quorum slices in SCP and how validators choose which nodes to trust.

content.prompt: In the Stellar Consensus Protocol, what is a 'quorum slice'?
options: The subset of nodes a validator chooses to trust when reaching agreement
The fraction of XLM required to vote in governance
The percentage of the total supply held by the Stellar Foundation
A batch of transactions bundled into one ledger entry

solution: The subset of nodes a validator chooses to trust when reaching agreement
hint: Each validator picks its own trusted set; overlapping quorum slices create global consensus.
author: StellarHuntsTeam

title: Ledger Close Time
description: Discover how fast the Stellar network finalizes transactions compared to Proof-of-Work blockchains.

content.prompt: Approximately how often does the Stellar network close a new ledger (finalize a batch of transactions)?

hint: Stellar is designed for speed — its consensus is much faster than Bitcoin's 10-minute block time.
author: StellarHuntsTeam
